coverage_summary: All nine trajectories were reviewed against the supplied paper text, including preprocessing, pretraining objectives, reconstruction, classification, clustering, perturbation profiling, batch correction, HPA aggregation, and multichannel representation assembly.

findings.detail: The padding step has no bypass for already-square images, although the paper limits zero-padding to segmented images that are not square. The current graph therefore implies unconditional padding.

evidence.quote: When segmented cell images did not conform to a square shape, zero-padding was applied to obtain square inputs.

findings.required_change: Add an already-square bypass or otherwise encode the documented condition.

findings.detail: Hard-negative mining is bound only to structured captions. The paper describes selecting unmatched image-text pairs, so the caption-only binding is unsupported.

evidence.quote: Hard negative mining is applied to select informative unmatched pairs.

findings.required_change: Represent the candidate image-text pair context or leave the opaque mining boundary without asserting a caption-only input.

findings.detail: The ITM step binds a separately produced caption embedding, but the cited ITM description specifies query logits for matched image-text pairs and does not establish this caption-embedding port or its use in the classifier.

evidence.quote: ITM is a binary classification task that determines whether an image-text pair is matched or not.
For each output query embedding, a linear classifier produces a logit.

findings.required_change: Remove the unsupported caption-embedding binding or represent the documented text-conditioned pair-processing boundary without inventing its tensor interface.

findings.detail: The reconstruction graph gives unmasked_visual_memory a compact n_visible_tokens axis, but the equation only establishes element-wise masking and the paper does not state whether the retained memory is compacted or remains a masked full-length sequence.

evidence.quote: producing masked features X masked = X ⨀ (1 - M).
the masked tokens are reconstructed using cross-attention to the unmasked memory from the image encoder.

findings.required_change: Leave the memory layout unspecified or represent the full-length masked sequence with an explicit mask; do not assert n_visible_tokens without evidence.

findings.detail: The reconstruction and alignment routes use distinct query-resource nodes despite the paper stating that the reconstruction pathway shares parameters with the image-text alignment Q-Former. The graph records textual sharing but does not establish shared resource identity.

evidence.quote: the reconstruction pathway shares parameters with the image-text alignment Q-Former

findings.required_change: Bind both routes to the same documented Q-Former/query parameter resource or add an explicit shared-parameter relation.

findings.detail: The graph contains separate alignment and reconstruction losses/objective states but no documented joint optimization step connecting all four objectives. The paper explicitly defines a joint pretraining objective.

evidence.quote: The four pre-training objectives ... are jointly optimized during pre-training.
The reconstruction objective is weighted by a scalar coefficient and jointly optimized with the image-text alignment objectives during pretraining.

findings.required_change: Add an opaque joint-objective/optimization boundary preserving the four objectives and the reconstruction weighting coefficient.

findings.detail: The classification preprocessing route lacks the documented exceptions for DIBaS and CM4AI. Its only bypass is the generic already-single-cell condition, while the paper states that these full-field datasets also skipped segmentation.

evidence.quote: Full-field images were processed using the same preprocessing pipeline as in pretraining ... except for DIBaS ... and CM4AI ...; neither dataset underwent single-cell segmentation.

findings.required_change: Add explicit DIBaS and CM4AI no-segmentation bypasses.

findings.detail: The classification trajectory omits the documented multichannel route: independent per-channel feature extraction followed by concatenation. This matters for the multichannel evaluation datasets represented by the classification input node.

evidence.quote: For multi-channel microscopy images, features are extracted independently from each channel using the same procedure.
The resulting channel-specific feature vectors are then concatenated to form the final image representation.

findings.required_change: Connect classification inputs with multiple channels to the documented channelwise extraction and concatenation path, or explicitly mark that path as the shared upstream boundary.

findings.detail: classification_scores is shaped only as n_classes, omitting the sample/image axis expected when the classifier is applied to image-level features.

evidence.quote: The Q-Former outputs a fixed set of 32 query embeddings for each image.
a unified classifier architecture is adopted, consisting of a 128-dimensional hidden layer followed by a classification layer.

findings.required_change: Represent classification scores with a sample/image axis, such as n_images by n_classes.

findings.detail: The perturbation trajectory collapses a documented encoder, Q-Former, and query-mean sequence into one opaque extraction step, although the paper states the ordered operations and their output representation.

evidence.quote: All images are subsequently processed by the pretrained image encoder and Q-Former to extract visual representations.
we compute the mean of the query embeddings, resulting in a single 768-dimensional feature vector per image.

findings.required_change: Decompose or reference the documented image-encoder, Q-Former, and query-mean stages before perturbation aggregation.

findings.detail: The perturbation aggregation steps have no image-to-well or well-to-treatment grouping operands. The source makes these correspondences essential to the well and treatment representations.

evidence.quote: welllevel representations are computed by averaging image-level features
aggregating wells subjected to identical perturbation conditions

findings.required_change: Add grouping-key/context nodes for image-site-to-well and well-to-treatment correspondence, or explicitly preserve them as unresolved selectors.

findings.detail: The results describe site-, well-, and treatment-level representations, while the trajectory contains image-, well-, and treatment-level nodes without documenting whether image-level and site-level are equivalent.

evidence.quote: hierarchically aggregated to derive site-, well-, and treatment-level representations
Image-level features are obtained by average aggregation of single-cell features.

findings.required_change: Add a site-level node or explicitly document the image-level/site-level equivalence used by this trajectory.

findings.detail: The batch-distance step uses only image features, although IMAD requires distances measured across experimental batches. No batch or plate identifier context is represented.

evidence.quote: Batch-related variability is quantified using the Inverse Median Absolute Deviation (IMAD)
feature distances measured across experimental batches

findings.required_change: Add batch/plate identifiers or an explicit batch-correspondence context operand to the distance and IMAD boundaries.

findings.detail: The clustering trajectory starts from raw evaluation images and hides preprocessing exceptions documented for DIBaS and CM4AI. The graph therefore does not preserve the dataset-specific input branches.

evidence.quote: Full-field images were processed using the same preprocessing pipeline as in pretraining ... except for DIBaS ... and CM4AI ...; neither dataset underwent single-cell segmentation.
For unsupervised evaluation, KMeans clustering is applied to image representations extracted from all datasets.

findings.required_change: Add the documented segmentation and no-segmentation branches before clustering representation extraction.

findings.detail: The HPA aggregation step receives only feature values, while the paper explicitly groups by cell line, protein localization, and protein identity. Those grouping keys are absent from the graph.

evidence.quote: single-cell images are grouped according to cell line, protein localization, and protein identity.

findings.required_change: Add the three grouping-key/context operands or represent the grouping boundary with explicit unresolved selectors.

findings.detail: The HPA trajectory also collapses the documented feature-extraction sequence into an opaque boundary despite the general preprocessing section specifying image encoder, Q-Former, query averaging, and multichannel handling.

evidence.quote: All images are subsequently processed by the pretrained image encoder and Q-Former to extract visual representations.
we compute the mean of the query embeddings

findings.required_change: Decompose or reference the documented shared feature-extraction stages before HPA grouping.

findings.detail: The paper contains a trainability contradiction that the graph does not preserve: the image encoder is described as frozen in the encoder and architecture sections, while the training protocol says the full architecture is optimized end-to-end.

evidence.quote: Freezing the image encoder
The full scMIR architecture ... is optimized end-to-end.
the image encoder ... remains unchanged throughout this work.

findings.required_change: Record the contradiction and retain the source-supported uncertainty about image-encoder trainability rather than asserting only the frozen interpretation.
